text:
Marathon Petroleum fell 0.6% today after releasing its quarterly earnings report and announcing a leadership change. The stock has been volatile over the past two weeks, swinging between gains and losses, and today's decline caps a 9.94% drop since late October. With oil prices holding steady around $103/barrel domestically and refineries running at 92.8% capacity, the move appears tied to market reaction to the company's financial results and forward guidance rather than a shift in refining fundamentals.

The broader context matters here: a CNBC report from earlier this week cautioned that Big Oil earnings guidance—not just reported profits—could disappoint investors, and market reaction to leadership changes can add uncertainty even when operational metrics remain solid. Refinery utilization remains healthy and inventory levels are stable, so today's decline likely reflects investor concerns about what the company sees ahead rather than current conditions.
